newsitem.title: UK: Burmah Castrol to close U.S. blending plant.
newsitem.headline: Burmah Castrol to close U.S. blending plant.

text.p: Lubricants maker Burmah Castrol Plc said on Monday it plans to close its blending plant in New Jersey this summer in a bid to fight tough market conditions in the U.S.
The closure of the plant, which employs around 60, will result in an exceptional charge of about $10 million, chief executive Jonathan Fry told journalists.
Fry could not say how many employees would have to leave, adding that some will be redeployed elsewhere within Burmah Castrol.
The company will outsource the blending to a nearby factory of Exxon Corp.
Fry said Burmah did not plan any closures in Europe where it was much harder to lay off staff.

Instead, the company wants to fight increased competition and sluggish markets here through such measures as standardising information technology and packaging as well as combining purchasing and distribution across the continent.
While Fry said he saw some slight improvements in the U.S. market recently, he doubted there would be much change in this year's conditions in Europe.

Here, Burmah has maintained its share in the lubricants market at around 10 percent, but was feeling the effects of last year's European downstream mega-merger between Mobil Corp and British Petroleum Co Plc.
Mobil and BP have a combined market share of around 18 percent. Both companies's lubricants are now aggressively marketed under the Mobil brand name, Fry said.
Burmah earlier reported a 10 percent increase in its 1996 profit after tax of 148.7 million pounds, which was more than expected due to one-off tax benefits.
